translations.text: When she could no longer hide him, she took a basket of rushes, coated it with bitumen and pitch, put the child in it, and placed it in the marsh by the riverbank.
His sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Shall I go and call a nursing woman from among the Hebrew women to nurse this child for you?”
He said to him, “Who made you a ruler and judge over us? Do you intend to kill me as you killed that Egyptian yesterday?” Moses was afraid and said, “Surely the matter has become known.”
The Lord said to him, “What is that in your hand?” He said, “A staff.”
The Lord said to him, “Put your hand back inside your clothing.” He put his hand back inside his clothing and brought it out, and it had become like the rest of his flesh.
Zipporah took a flint and cut off her son’s foreskin. She took hold of his feet and said, “I have a bridegroom of blood.”
The taskmasters pressed them, saying, “Complete your work as you always did, as when straw was given to you.”
Pharaoh said to them, “You are idle, utterly idle! That is why you say, ‘Let us go and sacrifice to the Lord.’”
Go and tell Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to send the Israelites out of his land.
Moses said to the Lord, “Look, the Israelites do not listen to me. How will Pharaoh listen to me, when my tongue stammers?”
Aaron raised his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.
The Lord did as Moses had said, and the frogs died in the houses, the courtyards, and the fields.
The Lord said to Moses, “Raise your hand toward heaven, and there will be hail throughout the land of Egypt, on people and livestock and on all the plants in the fields in the land of Egypt.”
The flax and barley were destroyed, because the barley had formed ears and the flax had formed bolls.
No one could see anyone else, and no one rose from his place for three days. But all the Israelites had light where they lived.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he was unwilling to send them away.
Moses and Aaron performed these wonders before Pharaoh. But the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not send the Israelites out of his land.
This month will be the beginning of the months for you. It will be the first of all the months of the year for you.
And when your children say to you, “What is this ceremony?”
The Lord said to Moses.
Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp at the mouth of the canal, between Migdol and the sea, in front of Baal-zephon. You are to camp opposite it, beside the sea.
He bound the wheels of their chariots, and they drove them with difficulty. The Egyptians said, “Let us flee from the Israelites, because the Lord is fighting for them against Egypt.”
The Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the sea, and the waters will return over the Egyptians, over their chariots and their horsemen.”
You blew with your wind, and the sea covered them. They sank like lead in the mighty waters.
The peoples heard and trembled; fear seized the inhabitants of Philistia.
Moses prayed before the Lord, and the Lord showed him a piece of wood. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There he taught him laws and judgments, and there he tested him.
When Aaron spoke to the whole congregation of the Israelites, they turned toward the wilderness, and there the glory of the Lord appeared in the cloud.
The mist of dew lifted, and there on the surface of the wilderness was a thin, flaky substance, crusted like ice on the ground.
They gathered it every morning, each person as much as he could eat. When the sun grew hot, it melted.
On the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two measures for each person. All the elders of the congregation came and told Moses.
They left some of it until morning, as Moses had commanded them, and it did not spoil, nor were there worms in it.
Moses said to them, "Eat it today, because today is a Sabbath to the Lord. Today you will not find it in the field."
On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather it, but they found none.
Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he told him.
In the third month after the Israelites came out of Egypt, on that very day, they came to the wilderness of Sin.
They set out from Rephidim and came to the wilderness of Sinai. They camped in the wilderness, and Israel camped there opposite the mountain.
The Lord said to Moses, "Go down and warn the people not to go too far before the Lord to see him, lest many of them fall."
If he does not do these three things for her, she shall go free without any payment of money.
When a man strikes his male or female slave with a rod, and the slave dies under his hand, he must be punished.
An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, a foot for a foot.
When a man strikes the eye of his male or female slave and destroys it, he shall set the slave free in compensation for the eye.
If an ox gores a son or a daughter, it shall be dealt with according to this judgment.
If an ox gores a male or female slave, its owner shall give thirty silver staters to the slave's master, and the ox shall be stoned.
When a man gives his neighbor money or articles for safekeeping, and they are stolen from the man's house, if the thief is found, he shall repay double.
Be careful to observe everything I have told you. Do not mention the names of other gods, and do not let them enter your thoughts.
Moses took the blood and sprinkled it on the people, and said, "This is the blood of the covenant that the Lord has made with you concerning all these words."
This is the offering you shall receive from them: gold, silver, and bronze.
Insert the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, so that the ark may be carried with them.
The cherubim shall spread their wings upward, covering the atonement cover with their wings. Their faces shall face one another; the faces of the cherubim shall be above the atonement cover.
Make a grating of bronze mesh, and make four bronze rings on the grating, on its four sides.
Bring the bull before the tent of meeting, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the bull’s head.
Take some of the bull’s blood and sprinkle it on the horns of the altar with your finger. Pour out all the blood at the base of the altar.
Burn the bull’s flesh, its hide, and its dung in the fire outside the camp. It is a sin offering.
And one loaf of bread, one loaf of bread made with oil, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the Lord.
Take them from their hands, and offer the breast of the ram on the altar as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma before the Lord. It is an offering to the Lord.
Overlay it with pure gold—its top, its sides all around, and its horns. Make a gold molding around it.
Take for yourself the finest spices: five hundred of pure myrrh; half as much fragrant cinnamon, two hundred and fifty; and two hundred and fifty of fragrant cane.
Keep the Sabbath, because it is holy to you. Whoever profanes it must be put to death. Whoever does work on it shall be cut off from his people.
The Lord said to Moses, “I have seen this people, and look, they are a stubborn people.”
“Now leave me alone, so that my anger may burn against them and I may destroy them. I will make you into a great nation.”
Moses returned to the Lord and said, “Please, Lord God! This people has indeed committed a great sin and made gods of gold for themselves.”

He said, “I will make all my goodness pass before you, and I will proclaim the name of the Lord before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy.”
The Lord said to Moses, “Here is a place beside me. Stand on the rock.”
Celebrate the Festival of Weeks at the beginning of the wheat harvest, and the Festival of Ingathering at the end of the year.
Whenever Moses went in before the Lord to speak with him, he would remove the veil until he came out. Then he would come out and tell the people of Israel what he had been commanded.
All the skilled craftsmen doing the work made the tabernacle with ten curtains of spun fine linen, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn. They made them with cherubim, the work of a skilled craftsman.
There were eight boards and sixteen silver bases for them: two bases under one board and two bases under another board.
He made a rim a handbreadth wide around it, and made a gold molding around its rim.
A shekel per person, half a shekel according to the sanctuary weights, for everyone counted in the census, from twenty years old and upward: six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
All the bronze contributed as an offering was seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels.
The waistband of the ephod was made as one piece with it, with the same workmanship: gold, blue, purple, scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The fourth row: chrysolite, beryl, and jasper. They were enclosed and set entirely in gold.
They attached the two braided chains at the two ends to the two settings, and attached them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at its front.
They made woven tunics of fine linen for Aaron and his sons.
They brought the tabernacle to Moses: the tent and all its equipment, its loops, its clasps, its boards, its pegs, its bars, its pillars, and its bases.
Just as the Lord commanded Moses, so the Israelites did all the work.
Moses did everything the Lord commanded him; that is what he did.
